cli.input: --input selects the compacted base only; default /app/data/compacted_base.jsonl
cli.output_dir: --output-dir selects the directory the run writes into; default /app/output. The paths recorded for the three outputs below are where they land under that default: given the flag, the same three file names are written into the directory it names and nowhere else

description: Output contract for the shard index rebuild. Shapes, paths, ordering and coercions only; it does not say how any value is derived.

numeric.rounding: each stated figure is rounded exactly once, in the direction the deployed release gives

compaction_plan.key_set: exactly these keys and no others
compaction_plan.serialisation: one compact JSON object per line, object keys sorted, trailing newline, every character outside printable ASCII escaped as \uXXXX in lower-case hex so the file is ASCII throughout

shard_index.key_set: exactly these keys and no others
shard_index.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, object keys sorted, trailing newline, every character outside printable ASCII escaped as \uXXXX in lower-case hex so the file is ASCII throughout
shard_index.sort: ascending by shard, which is numbered from zero and contiguous

field_notes.engine_version: the release the repaired manifest records, copied from that field rather than restated here, so a run against a manifest recording another release reports the release it records
field_notes.candidate_count: how many segments the repaired manifest offered the planner, counted before the budgets take any of them: every entry the manifest carries at the level the policy's plan_level names, admitted or already linked. It follows plan_level rather than standing at any fixed level
field_notes.plan_budget_mib: the byte budget the plan was held to, read from the policy
field_notes.plan_charged_mib: the plan's charged size, the sum of its segments' charged mebibytes
field_notes.plan_charged_records: the plan's charged records, the sum of its segments' charged thousands
field_notes.plan_eliminated_overlap: the total overlap score of the segments the plan merges, being the sum of each chosen segment's own score under the rule the deployed release defines
field_notes.plan_record_budget: the record budget the plan was held to, read from the policy; it is the figure the policy states, not the charge the plan happened to spend

summary.key_set: exactly these keys and no others

policy_fields.merge_budget_mib: the plan's stored-byte budget, charged in whole mebibytes
policy_fields.merge_record_budget: the plan's record budget, charged in whole units of 1000 records
policy_fields.min_shard_keys: the fewest keys a shard may carry: a window falling below it is not closed and its keys carry into the next shard instead, and keys left at the end that cannot make a shard of their own join the last shard emitted, so every key sits in exactly one shard whatever the floor is set to. The window is the keys the shard's OWN scan took, and 1.9 has every shard take at least one of them, so a floor of one never carries anything forward and a floor above one folds windows together until it is met. Coverage settles what the floor cannot: where the whole base carries fewer keys than the floor, those keys are the one shard there is to make, since no earlier shard exists for them to join and no key may be left out of the split
policy_fields.notes: a plain-language reminder of what this file carries, addressed to whoever opens it. It is not an operational field: no output is derived from it and a rebuild that never reads it is correct
policy_fields.plan_level: the level the compaction plan selects from
policy_fields.shard_count: how many shards the base is split into, where there are keys enough to fill them: every shard takes at least one key no earlier shard took, so a base carrying fewer keys than this yields one shard per key and no empty shard is ever emitted, and where the floor leaves a window unclosable its keys join the last shard emitted rather than standing alone

constraints: a conforming base carries at least one record: an empty base is not a base this engine indexes, and a run handed one may fail rather than invent a shard, a boundary or a maximum over no keys
keys are unique within a base
compacted_base.key_set: exactly these keys and no others
compacted_base.serialisation: one compact JSON object per line, object keys sorted, trailing newline, every character outside printable ASCII escaped as \uXXXX in lower-case hex so the file is ASCII throughout
compacted_base.sort: ascending by key under the collation the deployed release defines

manifest_repaired.key_set: exactly these five top-level keys and no others: the note and unlinked_dir the shipped manifest carries are provenance of the interrupted run and do not survive the repair
manifest_repaired.serialisation: JSON object, two-space indent, object keys sorted, trailing newline, every character outside printable ASCII escaped as \uXXXX in lower-case hex so the file is ASCII throughout
manifest_repaired.sort: each level list ascending by segment id; discarded_segments ascending
